verses.1: And Eliaši’b, the high priest, and his brothers, the priests, built the gate of the sanctuary. This gate was set apart as a holy place. They also repaired its doors. From the top of the tower, this gate remained a holy place until the time of Hanan’el.
verses.2: And by his hand, we begotten were the people of Yerho; and by his hand, he created a memory for his daughter Imri.
verses.3: And the gate of the animals was made by the sons of Sem. They repaired it, and they made its doors and locks workable.
verses.4: And on their shoulders was Meremoth, son of Uriah, son of Hacox. And on their shoulders was Meshulam, son of Berechiah, son of Mesizabael. And on their shoulders was Zadok, son of Baana.
verses.5: And on their hands, they carried the scepters and their authority; but they did not bring their commands into effect at their courts.
verses.6: And the door of the old house was kept by Yo’yada son of Paseh, and Meshulam son of Besodya. They guarded it, and locked its doors and gates.
verses.7: And on their shoulders they carried the heavy burdens. They also held the hammers used for cutting stones. These people were from Giv’on and Mitzpah, who lived beyond the river.
verses.8: By his hand, Euziel, son of Harahya, held the scepter. And by his hand, Hananiah, son of Harakhim, also held power. They left Jerusalem until they reached the vast wilderness.
verses.9: And by their side was Rephaiah, son of Hur, the chief officer in Jerusalem.
verses.10: And on their hands, they would hold Yedaya ben-Harumpa’s hands. And against his house, they would hold Chatush ben-Chashbaniya’s hands.
verses.11: For the second time, Malchiah will hold the throne, along with Hashub, son of Pachath Moab. And he will also be the ruler over the Tannaim.
verses.12: And in his hands, he held Shalom, the son of the high priest of Jerusalem. He and his descendants were also under his control.
verses.13: The gate of the Gaiya is held by Hanun, and those who reside in Zanocha built it. They sealed its doors and gates, and over a thousand years passed until the gate of the Shafot was opened.
verses.14: And the gate of the ashpoth was kept by Malchiyah ben Rekhav, the chief priest of the house of the krām. He built it, and set up its doors and locks.
verses.15: And he held the gate of the inner courtyard. Shalun, son of Kall-Hozah, the governor of the palace, built it and prayed for its protection. He also sealed its doors with locks, and protected it from all threats. And he also protected the garden of the king, as well as those who came from the city of David.
verses.16: After him, Nehemiah, son of Azbuk, became the governor of half of the province of Beth-Zur. He served until near the tombs of David, and also until the time when the priests were ordained to their positions.
verses.17: After him, the Levites held in their hands the tablets of judgment. On those tablets were written the names of the rulers who ruled over half of the land.
verses.18: After them, their relatives held Waya Ben-Hanadad, the head of half a phyle.
verses.19: And he strengthened Ezri son of Jesse, the commander of the army, once again, against the enemy forces that were attacking from above.
verses.20: After that, he held the blessed son of Zakhai once again, from the very top down to the entrance of Eliashiv’s house.
verses.21: After that, he held Meromot, son of Uria, from the entrance of the house of Eliezer, all the way up to the end of the house of Eliezer.
verses.22: And after them, the priests and the people of the Temple took control.
verses.23: After him, Neiman and Hashuv ruled over their homes. After them, Azariah son of Maaseya ruled over his home.
verses.24: After that, he held the position of governor for Banu Khandad for a second time, from the house of Azariah to the extreme limits and beyond.
verses.25: Forbode not Balaam, son of Ozzai, against the high and great one who comes from the house of the king. Next to him is Pedaiah, son of Pharets.
verses.26: And the singers sat in rows, facing the gate of the sea towards the east and the hill that led there.
verses.27: After that, they held the handles from two sides, along the entire length of the large platform, from the beginning to the end.
verses.28: Above the gates of the horses, the priests stood, with each of them facing a different direction.
verses.29: After him, Zadok held the position of son of Immer, opposite his house. And after him, Shemaiah, son of Shkanya, was in charge of guarding the gate of Mizra.
verses.30: After him, Hananiah son of Shelmeah and Hanan son of Zalaf the Shishi from Midah were in charge. After them, Mesulam son of Berechya was in charge, facing Nishatok.
verses.31: After him, Malchiah held the position of ruler until he reached the house of the administrators and those who were in charge of the gates. He also continued to hold this position until he reached the top of the hill.
verses.32: And on the upper part of the entrance to the sheep pen, the guards and watchmen stood guard.
verses.33: And when Sanbalat heard that we were building the temple, he became very angry. He was extremely upset and laughed at the Jews.
verses.34: And he said before his brothers and the army of Shomron, “What are these wicked Jews doing? They want to abandon them, to worship idols. They’ve taken stones from the mountains and made them into idols.”
verses.35: And the good man lived with him. He also said, “When they build there, may a flood come and destroy their homes.”
verses.36: Hear our God, for we have been in such a state of disgrace. Let their shame return to them, and let them be punished in the land of Shivya.
verses.37: And do not cover their sins and faults before you. Do not punish them, for they have acted against the laws of God.
verses.38: And the house was built, and all of it was connected until half of it was completed. It became a place where people could live in peace.
